the coil as a coworker tried to slow the coil's fall but it trapped his foot
underneath it  The employee was killed from blunt force trauma.
At 2:00 p.m. on February 4, 2020, an employee working as a machine operator for
a warehouse supercenter was crushing boxes in the BACE Model V63 Bailer and
Compaction Equipment. The bailer had been rented from an outside equipment
supplier and was installed at no cost to the company in exchange for a
discounted price on their recycled materials. The outside supplier was
responsible for maintenance for any problems resulting from normal wear and
tear. There were no reported maintenance issues with the bailer at the time. The
Bailer had an interlock mechanism that is supposed to prevent employees from
getting their hands caught in the point of operation.  The employee stated that
as he was crushing the boxes, some cardboard was sticking out of the machine. He
tried to push the cardboard back into the machine when his left hand became
caught in the bailer while it was operating. The employee amputated his middle
and ring fingers, requiring hospitalization. It is not currently known why the
interlock did not prevent the incident, but the machine was taken out of
service.
At 7:34 a.m. on January 14, 2020, an employee was riding on the lift installed
on a trailer. The employee's left foot was protruding over the lift platform,
and, as the lift raised toward the trailer, the employee's foot got caught in
the gap. This resulted in the amputation of digits 2 and 3 to the first joint on
left foot and was treated without requiring hospitalization.
At 8:55 a.m. on August 29, 2019, Employee #1 was working inside a new residence
being constructed.  He was using a powered hand held circular saw to cut a 2 by
6 piece of lumber.  The saw kicked back, striking and amputating the tip of the
employee's left thumb.   The employee was hospitalized for treatment of the
amputation.
At 6:00 a.m. on February 3, 2020, an employee was stacking cut countertops.  The
employee tried to clean dirt and grease from a rotating sprocket and chain. The
employee amputated his fingertip and was hospitalized.
At 1:30 p.m. on January 28, 2020, Employee #1,  a temporary employee, was
working on a high speed production line and was filling 12 ounce bottles with a
car windshield cleaning product, TBS-C15A, a flammable liquid from a 55 gallon
drum. The employee was using a motorized pump with a hose to transfer the
product to the bottles when he began to have difficulty with pumping out the
remainder of the product at the bottom of the drum due to the hose being too
short. The employee manually picked up the 55 gallon drum and attempted to dump
the excess product into another 55 gallon drum designated to collect excess
product. While the employee was transferring the excess, an explosion occurred.
The employee was treated at the hospital and released the same day for 2nd
degree burns to his hands. Employee #2 was working inside the packaging area and
was hospitalized to treat 2nd degree burns to her arms, hands, and face.
Employee #3,  a temporary employee, was affected and hospitalized to treat 2nd
degree burns to her hand, arms, and face. It was determined that the drums were
not grounded and that the product is only run once per month so employees have
less experience with this product.
At 1:45 p.m. on January 20, 2020, an employee was cutting neck bones with a
bandsaw when his right index finger contacted the saw blade. The employe
amputated his fingertip, requiring medical treatment without hospitalization.
At 2:45 p.m. on February 4, 2020, an employee was talking to the truck driver
and was standing in a blind spot.  The employee was struck by a truck and was
killed.
At 2:00 p.m. on February 4, 2020, an employee working in an administrative
support position for a government executive office was walking into an office.
The employee caught the edge of her foot while turning and as she fell, she put
her arm out to catch herself. The employee fractured her arm and injured her
shoulder and was hospitalized.
At 4:00 p.m. on January 31, 2020, an employee was working as a welder, tasked
with moving an idle roller with a forklift used for stability of ships for
welding operations. As he was positioning dunnage under the idle rollers for the
forklift, the idle roller slipped, crushing his left foot. The employee was sent
to the hospital, where the tip of his left big toe was surgically amputated. The
employee was hospitalized.
At 6:55 a.m. on January 31, 2020, Employee #1, a male employee, was removing the
back plate from a horizontal casting tundish furnace.  The molten bronze,
plugging one of the dies, let loose and released molten bronze out of the die.
The employee was struck in the leg with 2,200-degree molten metal and sustained
second and third degree burns to his right leg and foot.  Employee #1 was
of a machine head. The employee climbed through the machine head hatch to access
the top of the equipment. As the employee stepped from one machine head to
another machine she fell to the ground. The employee fractured her back, foot,
ankle and hip after and required hospitalization.
At 9:45 p.m. on February 5, 2020, an employee working as an engineering
technician for an express delivery service was performing maintenance on a
conveyor belt. The employee was working on relieving tension in the belt when he
got his left thumb caught between the belt and the roller. The employee partial
amputated his thumb through the phalanx and required medical treatment without
hospitalization.
At 9:45 p.m. on February 5, 2020, an employee working as an engineering
technician for an express delivery service was performing maintenance on a
conveyor belt. The employee was working on relieving tension in the belt when he
got his left thumb caught between the belt and the roller. The employee partial
amputated his thumb through the phalanx and required medical treatment without
hospitalization.
At 6:00 a.m. on February 14, 2020, Employee #1 and Employee #2, employed by an
egg producing and processing company, were removing dead chickens from Tecno
cages. The cage structure collapsed. Employee #1 was crushed and killed under
the cages. Employee #2 received minor injuries and did not have to be
hospitalized.
At 4:30 p.m. on November 13, 2019, an employee was working at a slaughterhouse.
He was working on the facility's "final rail," performing his normal job duties.
He was removing the bottom right leg of a hog. He was making the cut with a long
knife, when he misjudged the weight of the hog leg. The leg came down and
pressed the knife into the employee's left arm. The employee suffered a puncture
to or laceration of his left arm above the elbow. He was hospitalized.
At 10:00 a.m. on February 11, 2020, Employee #1 was descending a ladder from the
second story to the first story and fell off the ladder from the height of the
first story to the ground. Employee #1 suffered a broken arm and lacerations and
was hospitalized.
At 8:51 p.m. on October 3, 2019, an employee who worked as a heavy equipment
operator for a dry distribution logistics company was performing his typical
duties. The employee unloaded and loaded products daily. The facility is a
storage warehouse where operations involve use of equipment to store product on
shelves and loading and unloading trailers. The employee was operating a Crown
RC 5500 Series powered industrial vehicle (PIV). He was heading to case pick and
as he was coming down the aisle he had to turn the PIV around to place the forks
in front of him. As he turned the equipment he was ejected and thrown into the
rack. He stated that as the forklift started to come toward him he fell down and
the wheel drove over his foot crushing it. He used his radio to call for help
and a Coworker #1 (Supervisor) and Coworker #2 (Trainee) came to his aid
immediately. The employee crushed his foot and fractured his tibia and ankle. An
ambulance transported him to the hospital, where he was admitted to undergo
three surgeries. On October 10, 2019, he was discharged. Following discharge,
the employee has been undergoing physical therapy at his residence and according
to his doctor recovery could take 6 months to a year.
At 12:00 p.m. on February 7, 2020, Employee #1 was working from a ladder jack
scaffolding to prepare for a concrete pour. The ladder jack was setup on three
separate extension ladders. One of the ladders was not secured. As Employee #1
was working near the unsecured ladder, it shifted causing Employee #1 to fall
4-feet on to a concrete pier.  Employee #1 suffered six fractured ribs and was
hospitalized.
At 12:00 p.m. on February 17, 2020, Employee # 1, employed by a construction
roofing contractor, was trying to retrieve his knife from the edge of the roof.
Employee #1 unhooked his lanyard to grab the knife and then went to re-attach
his harness when he slipped and fell off the roof. Employee #1 fell 27 feet to
the ground.  Employee #1 fractured his back at vertebrae (C-7) and was
hospitalized.
At 8:00 a.m. on February 18, 2020, Employee #1 was employed by a construction
painting contractor.  Employee #1 fell 5.5 feet from a rolling scaffold and hit
his head on the surface below. Employee #1 was hospitalized.
At 7:45 a.m. on February 12, 2020, an employee had a coworker, a forklift
operator, lift a block cart with the forklift so he could hit the wheel caster
with a sledgehammer to straighten the wheel. As the employee struck the wheel
caster, the block cart shifted on the forks causing the base plate to fall off
the cart and hit him. The employee lost his balance and fell to the ground. The
employee was hospitalized to treat a fractured left femur.
At 11:00 a.m. on September 19, 2019, an employee was using a sweeper in an
almond field.  As the employee attempted to turn off the sweeper blow unit from
his balance and grabbed hold of the strap that held the boxes in place instead
of the handle used to climb the truck. The strap snapped and the employee fell
backwards approximately 4 feet and landed and hit his head on the concrete
floor.  The employee suffered head trauma, bruising and lacerations that
required inpatient hospitalization for four days.
At 4:30 p.m. on March 20, 2020, an employee was operating a tube cutting laser.
While operating a LT Fiber Laser, he noticed that the next tube to be loaded
into the laser's chuck needed to be flipped to ensure that the weld seam was
upright. The employee opened up the sliding door on the machine, once the
machine had stopped. When the employee was within the machine, the chuck
carriage retracted to grab the next tube. The employee's forearm was caught
between the chuck carriage and the machine's frame. The employee was transported
to the hospital with a fractured radius and laceration injury. The employee was
hospitalized.  The machine's interlocked door was bypassed at the time of the
incident.
At 11:45 a.m. on March 13, 2020, Employee #1 was assisting in the
maintenance/servicing of a saw.  Employee #1 was assisting a coworker in
repairing an air leak on the saw. The equipment had not been locked out prior to
removing the guard. As Employee #1 reached his hand into the machine to check an
airline, his hand made contact with the still rotating saw blade. Employee #1
suffered an amputation of the right middle finger and was hospitalized.
At 6:45 a.m on March 19, 2020, an employee was walking to her lift truck after
clocking in for the day. It was unknown, but the employee stated that her leg
gave out on her, and fell.  The employee broke her femur and later died after
surgery.
At 2:30 p.m. on February 6, 2020, Employee #1 was cutting a hole in the plenum
of an HVAC unit.  Employee #1 was stepping down off the HVAC unit to a
stepladder he had previously placed to retrieve rechargeable batteries for
cordless tools. Employee #1 did not know someone had moved the ladder.  When
Employee #1 stepped out for the ladder he fell 9-feet striking the equipment
door that was open and landing on the concrete floor.  Employee #1 was
hospitalized to treat a fractured foot.
At 2:00 p.m. on March 13, 2020, Employee #1 was working for a construction
pipeline contractor, while laying pipeline.  Employee #1 reached inside the pipe
to find the seam to correctly connect the next pipeline section. The pipe was
suspended by slings. Employee #1 was holding the pipe while it was being lowered
when his fingers were trapped between the two pieces of pipe.  Employee #1
suffered an amputation of the fingertip on the right index finger. Employee #1
received medical treatment but was not hospitalized.
At approximately 8:10 a.m. on March 18, 2020, an employee was unloading a
transport van.  Then, two pallets of books fell off the back of the transport
sent to the hospital by her primary employer, a temporary staffing agency. She
was working as a nurse in the Cardiac Tele 4 South unit at the hospital. On
April 1, 2020, she died. Her death was not related to her work activity, and
this was not an OSHA-covered fatality. Although a COVID-19 infection was
suspected, her COVID-19 test was negative. As there were two employers, there
were two inspections for this investigation. Inspection 1472245 was for the
hospital, and inspection 1472424 was for the temporary staffing agency.
At 12:00 noon on January 10, 2020, an employee was walking away after having
rigged a concrete pole that was being lifted by a gantry crane when the wire
rope of the crane broke and the pole fell and hit the employee in the back. The
employee was hospitalized to treat a fractured vertebrae.
At 10:45 a.m. on March 31, 2020, an ambulatory assistant who was exposed to
COVID-19 died.
At 4:30 p.m. on April 14, 2020, Employee #1 was performing normal job duties as
well as assisting with entrance screening of individuals entering the hospital.
Employee #1 contracted Covid-19 during the course of work and later died.
At 5:30 p.m. on March 10, 2020, Employee #1 was working for a framing
contractor, while installing a cornice on the exterior of residential home.
Employee #1 fell from a scaffold with no fall protection.  Employee #1 suffered
lacerations, fractures and was hospitalized.
At 11:45 a.m. on October 14, 2019, an employee who worked for a building
materials manufacturer was grabbing the handles on a hoist clamp moving cement
blocks. The clamps were situated in such a way that one of the clamps became
stuck on a steel bar.  When the employee tried to move the clamp by maneuvering
the lifting system, one of the clamps struck his right index finger crushing it
and sheared the finger on the steel bar. The employee amputated his fingertip
and required medical treatment without hospitalization.
Approximately at 2:15 p.m. on April 2, 2020, an employee set-up and began
operating a CNC machine. When the employee reached the boring process of the
operation, an aluminum part was ejected from the machine. The employee was
killed in a collision with the ejected part, the door, or both. The employee
sustained trauma to his head and to the left side of his torso.
An employee contracted COVID-19 and died at 1:00 p.m. on April 5, 2020.
An employee worked at a regional medical center. It was a general medical and
surgical hospital. He was exposed to COVID-19. He was admitted to a different
hospital. At 8:30 a.m. on April 9, 2020, he died of complications due to his
exposure to COVID-19. This was an OSHA-covered fatality.
At approximately 9:10 a.m. on April 10, 2020, an employee was mixing chemicals
to spray onto the grass. It was alleged that he accidentally ingested some
chemicals while trying to siphon a hose that resulted in poisoning, leading to a
stroke.  The employee died.
At 8:30 a.m. on October 22, 2019, an employee was working as an iron worker for
a structural steel and precast concrete contractor. The employee and a coworker
were in the process of aligning post tension cables into a 2,400-pound post
tension ram. The employee and the coworker were in separate boom lifts manually
controlling a tension ram suspended by a pulley system. The employee was located
on opposite sides of the ram. They were having hard time fitting all the cables
into the ram. The employee was pulling down on the cable toward the cable wheel
while the coworker was pulling on other side of cable to help with load of the
ram. When the employee pulled the cable, the cable jerked while the employee had
his right hand on the cable causing his hand to travel through the wheel. The
employee caught his pinky finger between the cable and cable wheel. The employee
had full manual control of the cable at the time. The employee partially
amputated his finger to the first knuckle, requiring medical treatment
(stitches) but no hospitalization.
An employee worked as a bus driver at a state university. He was symptomatic
while at work on March 16, 2020. He called in sick on March 17, 2020. He never
returned to the workplace. He was admitted to the hospital on March 22, 2020. He
tested positive for COVID-19 on March 28, 2020. That same day, he died at a care
facility. This was an OSHA-covered fatality.
At 10:00 a.m. on October 23, 2019, an employee was using a Delta jointer to cut
a joint into a piece of wood. The employee was passing the wood through the
jointer when his glove got caught and pulled into the rotating saw blade. The
employee suffered a laceration to the tip of his pinky finger and was treated
without hospitalization.
At 2:00 a.m. on November 12, 2019, an employee working for a maintenance
contractor was onsite at an electric power-generation plant. The employee worked
as the supervisor for a five-employee crew. The crew was tasked with performing
maintenance on one of five power turbines. The employee and his crew had done
similar work in the past. The crew was removing an engine (LMS100 Super Core)
that had malfunctioned from one of the units so that it could be replaced. The
crew was using a Bishop Lifting Products 755040 REV A crane, which was a newer
design that would preclude the need for wood blocking for supporting the load
during the lift. After the crew placed the pin on the lift fixture to center the
load, the crew partially lifted the engine to allow the removal of bolts and
other components. The crew inadvertently had placed the pin in the wrong
position and the engine and had not been centered causing the load to be
improperly rigged. This caused the crane to shift while attempting to disengage
the load causing it to strike the employee's foot. The employee was admitted to
the hospital on November 12, 2019, where he was treated for crushing injuries to
his foot. He was released on November 14, 2019.
At approximately 9:00 A.M. on April 9, 2020, an employee, working for an
electrical contractor, was working on a conduit installation. The employee was
laying out core drills in the riser electrical room on the first floor. The
employee fell through a partially opened shaft approximately 11 feet onto a
concrete terrace. The employee was hospitalized and treated for broken vertebrae
and paralysis from the chest down.
An employee worked as a respiratory therapist at a general medical and surgical
hospital. On March 12, 2020, she developed symptoms consistent with COVID-19.
From March 31, 2020 through April 6, 2020, she worked in the neonatal intensive
care unit (NICU), the pediatric care unit (PICU), pediatric oncology,
pediatrics, women's surgery, antepartum, the pediatric post-anesthesia care
unit, and other clinics. She died on April 8, 2020. She was not hospitalized.
This was an OSHA-covered fatality.
At 8:30 a.m. on April 11, 2020, Employee #1, employed by a roofing company, was
a cold storage warehouse was sealing a trailer. The employee was struck by a
tractor trailer and caught between the trailer and a dock plate. The employee
broke his legs and was hospitalized.
At 10:30 a.m. on March 6, 2020, Employee #1 was drilling a hole to install
rebar, and Employee #2 was cleaning debris on the ground. A preconstructed wall
was being lifted by a nearby crane. The wall broke from the rigging and fell
onto another wall that collapsed and struck Employee #1 and Employee #2.
Employee #1 suffered a head injury and was hospitalized.  Employee #2 suffered a
back injury and was hospitalized.
At 6:02 p.m. on September 18, 2019, an employee was strapping a stack of
warehouse rack beams. As the employee attempted to tie the rack beams, the beams
fell onto the employee, crushing him. The employee sustained injuries to his
left leg and knee, resulting in hospitalization.
At 8:45 a.m. on March 3, 2020, an employee working for an engineered wood
products manufacturer was cutting wood with a ReSaw saw. The employee placed his
foot in front of the saw while it was running and struck his foot with the
sawblade. The employee was hospitalized to treat a laceration to his foot.
At 5:02 a.m. on February 22, 2020, an employee and a coworker were walking
through the yard to their parked trucks when another coworker, driving a yard
goat, turned left around a blind corner. The employee pushed the coworker out of
the way and the yard goat ran over his legs. The employee was hospitalized to
treat multiple fractures to both legs.
At 8:30 a.m. on March 5, 2020, an employee was working at a sewage treatment
facility. He and a coworker were removing an antenna from the roof of a building
at the wastewater treatment plant. The employee was getting ready to come back
down a portable extension ladder. The ladder did not extend the required three
rungs (3 feet, or 0.9 meters) above the roofline. The ladder was being supported
by the employee's colleague. As the employee attempted to get onto the ladder,
he missed the ladder rung. He fell 14 feet (4.3 meters). He suffered a
concussion and multiple fractures to his right radial bone (a bone in his
wrist). He was hospitalized. The employee was wearing only basic personal
protective equipment; that is, hard hat, safety shoes, and glasses. The employer
did not report the incident to the Division.
At 11:00 a.m. on March 4, 2020, Employee #1 was cutting a piece of wood on a
table saw. Employee #1 was using a DeWalt table saw with a missing guard, and
his finger got caught in the blade. Employee #1 sustained an amputation to the
left middle finger and was hospitalized.
At approximately 8:00 a.m. on March 8, 2020, an employee was smoothing a golf
sand bunker.  The employee became unconscious and fell to the ground.  The
employee was killed. The employee may have suffered cardiac arrest.
At 3:30 p.m. on March 9, 2020, Employee #1 was working for a structural steel
contractor.  Employee #1 was assisting with pile driving when he fell through a
unprotected roof hole.  Employee #1 fractured his collar bone, ribs, vertebrae
and head.  Employee #1 was hospitalized.
At 9:24 a.m. on March 6, 2020, an employee was working for a firm that was
engaged in general warehousing and storage. He worked in machinery maintenance.
He was working on a conveyor belt in the ECOMM or warehouse part of the
facility. At about 8:30 that morning, with a loud noise, an Automotion Live
Roller Conveyor System with part number CLRB-3479 had stopped running. The
employee was dispatched to get it running again. The chain in a section of the
conveyor system had broken. The conveyor system was shut off at the controls,
but it had not been locked out or tagged out at the energy source. The employee
had to get up on a lift to perform the necessary repair. He was installing the
master link and pin on the new chain when another employee turned the conveyor
system back on. In the investigation summary, it was said that the employee was
replacing a master pin in the gear box of the Daifuku conveyor, which apparently
was a part of the system. In either case, the employee's right hand was caught
in the conveyor's chain and sprocket. The employee suffered lacerations to his
second (index) finger, a laceration and fracture of his third (middle) finger,
At 1:30 p.m. on March 25, 2020, Employee #1 was installing an initial laying for
a roof top deck, during new project and addition construction.  He then
accidentally fell 60 feet from the upper deck to the ground and was killed.
At 8:40 a.m. on February 14, 2020, Employee # 1, was working from an extension
ladder applying plastic film to an elevated window to mask it prior to applying
the texturing compound. When he leaned to his right, the ladder shifted to the
left causing him to lose his balance and fall approximately 13 feet to the
plywood floor surface.  Coworker #1 heard  a noise from inside the house  and
when he investigated, he found Employee #1 lying on the floor in pain. He
reported the fall to Coworker #2 who immediately called 911 and went in to
monitor Employee #1 until EMS arrived.  Employee #1 suffered a fractured right
wrist and was admitted to the hospital for treatment.
At 9:30 a.m. on September 17, 2019, an employee was framing a single-family
track home.  The employee was using a hand operated skill saw to cut a 2 X 4
that was placed on a framed wall. The saw kicked back and amputated the
employee's left middle fingertip tip. The employee was treated without
hospitalization.
At 12:15 p.m. on March 18, 2020, an employee was using a Hobart food processor
to cut green peppers. The peppers had jammed, and the employee had pulled the
lever up and out to stop the blade.  Then, the employee reached inside the food
processor to move the peppers around.  The blade then started moving again,
while his hand was still inside. The employee's right-hand pointer and ring
fingers were amputated. The employee was treated without hospitalization.
At 9:30 a.m. on March 26, 2020, Employee #1, a construction flagger, was
conducting traffic control during a maintenance and repair project.  At this
time, an impaired driver drove their vehicle through the work zone and
accidentally struck Employee #1, currently working on foot, within the
construction site.  Afterwards, Employee #1 then sustained blunt force trauma
and other severe injuries and was killed.
At 11:14 p.m. on March 13, 2020, an employee was operating the DTR hose machine
producing automobile parts when her finger got caught in the machine clamp. The
employee was hospitalized to treat finger lacerations that led to amputation.
At 5:00 p.m. on February 5, 2020, four employees were involved in cutting an
I-beam. Employee #1 was atop a mezzanine cutting an I-beam with a cutting torch
while Employee #2 was also on the mezzanine as a fire watch. Employee #3 was on
the ground floor as a fire watch and Employee# 4 was on the ground floor
operating a forklift. As Employee #1 was cutting the I-beam, slag came down and
started as a small flame on the ground. Employee#3 attempted to put out the
flame with a hose and then a fire extinguisher. The fire spread and engulfed the
whole room. Employee#1 and Employee #2 suffered burns on multiple parts of
bodies and were hospitalized.
At 6:20 p.m. on November 5, 2019, an employee working as a Truck Driver for an
electric power generating company was tasked with driving a water truck. The
employee works with five coworkers, but his work as a Truck Driver requires
routinely working alone. The employee had just finished working for the day and
was being relieved by a coworker that he didn't normally work with who was not
familiar with the area. The employee was in the process of showing him where he
needed to go while the coworker followed in a separate vehicle. As the employee
started to drive down an approximate 13 percent grade hill, his truck slipped
out of gear. He applied the brakes but the truck wouldn't slow down. The
employee he panicked when he could not get the truck into gear nor get it to
stop, so he turned towards the steam lines on the side of the road to stop his
momentum. The steam lines were horizontal and vertical and when he hit the
vertical portion at approximately 35 to 40 miles per hour, the truck was heavily
damaged. The employee was pinned between the steering wheel and the seat until
help could arrive to free him. Due to his impact with the dashboard, he broke 6
ribs, fractured his sternum and his left hand/wrist was completely folded
backwards. He also sustained multiple contusions and abrasions and bruises. The
employee was hospitalized for treatment.
At 9:32 a.m. on December 23, 2019, an employee working as a laborer for a retail
home furniture business was working in a warehouse. The employee was working
with a coworker (owner) picking up supplies for a delivery.  The employee was
specifically picking out sheets of plywood to bring to the truck.  A 47-inch by
76-inch stack of plywood was leaned against a storage rack. The plywood ranged
from ?- to ?-inch in thickness and weighed approximately 24 pounds. They stacks
were stored with the long end in the vertical position. As the employee was
selecting amongst the stack of 15 sheets of plywood, it tipped and fell over on
top of him. The employee was hospitalized to treat a concussion, which left him
paralyzed and not able to talk.
At 6:32 am, on November 14, 2019, Employee #1 was hitching a trailer with a

be cranked high enough to reach the hitch, so Employee #1 manually lifted the
trailer to connect to the hitch.  When Employee #1 lowered the trailer, his left
pinky got caught between the trailer coupler and the hitch. Employee #1 suffered
installing shingles using a nail gun. Employee #1 fainted while working from a
personal medical problem.  Employee #1 received medical treatment but was not

On November 12, 2019, an employee was emptying trash from a truck in a garage
area.  The employee struck his knee on a hydraulic jack.  The employee's knee
became infected, and he was hospitalized for three days.
At 12:00 p.m. on May 7, 2020, Employee #1 and Employee #2 were on site to remove
a 35-foot tree. Employee #1 was in the tree with a chain saw, removing limbs and
lowering them to the ground to Employee #2, who was below the tree removing the
ropes from the limbs as they were lowered. The limbs were being lowered to the
ground by means of a rope over a limb from an adjacent tree. The adjacent tree
was not structurally sound, which caused it to fall over, striking Employee #2
and Employee #1. The employees suffered a broken back and leg, abrasions, and
bruising.  Two employees were hospitalized.
At 1:10 p.m. on April 14, 2020, an employee working as a sales driver for a
distribution center was working in Warehouse Aisle #20 moving headboards. The
employee was a regular full-time employee of the employer. The employee was
removing 10 75-pound headboards from a cart by using a Raymond Model 560-OPC30TT
Reach Truck at the end of the shift. As the employee was backing up the PIV, the
employee struck a box protruding from the storage rack with the load on the cart
causing the load to fall on him. The load was not properly secured or strapped
on the cart. The employee fractured his ribs, sustained lacerations and bruised
his liver, requiring hospitalization.
At 11:30 a.m. on April 18, 2020, an employee was working at a single-family
residence, dismantling and removing a wood gazebo from the back yard. During the
task, the employee cut small pieces from the top of the gazebo and removed a
horizontal member from the top portion of the gazebo.  As the employee pulled on
the top portion of the gazebo, the gazebo started to fall.  The employee ran
from his position under the gazebo into the direction the gazebo was falling and
was struck by the gazebo.  The employee sustained a fracture to the right tibia
and left forearm and was hospitalized.
At 4:00 p.m. on February 10, 2020, Employee #1 and a coworker were installing
drywall ceilings and walls for a multifamily unit under construction. They used
an eight-foot fiberglass step ladder with a 10-inch wood plank spanned between

vacuum truck boom struck a power line and the worker was killed by
electrocution.
At 2:51 p.m. on March 3, 2020, Employee #1 was employed by a construction
framing contractor.   He was working from job-made scaffold platform. Employee
#1 was performing framing work from job-made scaffold platform and fell to the
concrete floor below. Employee #1 suffered a head injury and was hospitalized.
At approximately 5:43 p.m. on March 16, 2020, an employee was spraying
pesticides while using a 2012 Honda FourTrax Rancher TRX420 in the vineyard. The
employee was  later found dead approximately six feet away from the vehicle
after an ATV roll-over.
At 9:50 a.m. on December 22, 2019, an employee working as an equipment operator
for a grocery wholesaler was operating a forklift. The employee crushed his
right foot and was transported to emergency room by ambulance. The employee was
released but scheduled for surgery on December 23, 2019. There were no known
witnesses and no other details available at the time the narrative was
submitted. Security video may be available. The employer is continuing to
investigate the accident which will require an interview of the employee once he
is able to speak to the employer.
At 11:00 a.m. on March 31, 2020, an employee working as an electrical lineman
for an electrical power distributor was climbing a utility pole to begin work on
an insulator. As the employee climbed the pole and approached the line, he
employee was using an incomplete scaffold with a ladder on top of it to do the
work. He and his coworkers had been performing in this manner for over a year.
The accident occurred as the employee was descending the A frame ladder that had
been placed on of the scaffold. He was carrying a siding board using both hands.
As he was coming down, the scaffold collapsed and the employee fell to the
ground.  The employee had several fractures in right arm and face, along with
neck and back pain and lacerations in face.  The employee was hospitalized.
At 12:30 p.m. on November 20, 2019, an employee was cutting meat with a vertical
meat cutting saw in the meat department.  The employee was cutting meat with a
vertical meat saw and failed to use the blade guard as required. The employee's
thumb came in contact with the unguarded blade, resulting in an amputation.  The
employee was treated at the hospital and released.
At 3:20 p.m. on May 10, 2020, Employee #1 and two coworkers were inspecting a
roof and securing roofing materials and tools due to an approaching storm.
Employee #1 was trying to secure a large sheet of PVC roofing membrane that had
become loose on the roof of the penthouse, located on top of the distribution
warehouse.  Employee #1 was laying on the membrane, when a strong gust of wind
lifted it up and flung the employee over the edge of the roof. Employee #1
suffered a broken wrist, fractured leg, torn tendon in knee, and a small
laceration between the eyes. Employee #1 was hospitalized.
At 12:00 a.m. on November 25, 2019, an employee was installing a mobile home.
While lifting the structure, the weight shifted. The employee sustained a
crushed left leg, and was hospitalized.
An employee was working as a certified nursing assistant (CNA) at an assisted
living facility for the elderly. She was working on a general care floor. On
April 16, 2020, she felt ill and began to experience symptoms of an infection
with COVID-19. On April 22, 2020, she was hospitalized. On April 29, 2020, she
died. The causes of her death were bronchial pneumonia, viral COVID-19, and
polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) COVID-19. This was an OSHA-covered fatality.
On January 15, 2020, an employee and three coworkers were erecting a
Freestanding Bridge Crane in the maintenance shop of a distribution warehouse.
The employee and coworkers attempted to orient a 28-foot steel beam, weighing
more than 1,400 pounds, which was to be used as a runway for the crane. The beam
was attached to the forks of a powered industrial trucks. The employee and one
of their coworkers were positioned on either side of the beam that was being
hoisted off the floor using a chain, two shouldered eyebolts, and two fasteners.
The beam became hung up on a chain link.  When the beam was released from the
hospitalized.
At 7:25 p.m. on March 7, 2020, an employee working as a machine operator for a
specialty wire manufacturer was setting up a wire machine when he caught his
finger under a strap. The employee amputated his left index fingertip and
required medical treatment without hospitalization.
At 12:30 p.m. on March 13, 2020, Employee #1, employed by an electrical services
company, was working from a ladder at a building construction project.  He was
using his bare hands to connect and splice electrical wiring to the electrical
panel box wiring while the wiring was energized to 120 volts.  The employee fell
from the ladder to the floor and then down a flight of stairs, a fall height of
24 feet.  Employee #1 was killed.
At 6:59 p.m. on July 16, 2019, Employee #1, employed by a welding and machine
repair company, was inside a shipping container on a trailer helping to unload a
shipment of electrical cabinets and panels. Employee #1 was behind the
electrical panel trying to push, as his coworker, a forklift operator, was
attempting to use a forklift to pull the 2,189 lb electrical panel out, endwise,
from the rear of the container.  Another forklift was in place to get a better
lift angle from the side, once the electrical panel was clear of the portal. As
the cabinet was being dragged, it suddenly tipped to the left side of the
container (looking in from the rear) and fell. It settled with the top edge of
the cabinet leaning against the left side of the container (looking in from the
rear) with approximately 3 feet of clearance from the top of the cabinet to the
container floor.   Employee #1 had moved to the side of the panel just before it
tipped over and he was struck by the cabinet and trapped due to other boxes in
the container blocking his exit forward and being too far from the open doors at
the rear of the container to escape. Employee #1 was struck on the head and
killed by the falling electrical cabinet. He was wearing a hard hat. He was
compressed vertically from standing to a seated position in the remaining 3 feet
clearance. A coroner determined that the falling electrical cabinet fractured
vertebrae in his neck.
At 11:00 a.m. on November 19, 2019, an employee working as a painter was
prepping for the repainting of existing two-story townhomes. The employee was
contracted to do the work by a painting contractor. The employee was masking a
balcony railing with Visqueen by covering the railing and securing it with
masking tape. The employee was reaching over the rail near one of the railing
posts when the wood cap on the top of the post came off the post. The employee
lost his balance and fell 12 feet over the rail onto the shrubs below. The
employee bruised his hip and shoulder and was transported to the hospital trauma
center. He was held overnight for observation and released the following morning
after less than 24 hours.
At 10:00 a.m. on February 25, 2020, an employee was operating a metal lathe.
The string from his hooded sweatshirt wrapped around the revolving part of the
lathe (300 RPM).  The employee was pulled into the machine. The employee was
hospitalized to treat a fractured collarbone, shoulder, right arm, and ribs.
The employee also sustained bruising, scrapes, lacerations, and a hematoma.
At 12:15 p.m. on March 16, 2020, Employees #1 and #2, employed by a mobile home
company, were working together at a multiemployer construction project.
Employee #1 was installing a hydraulic jack underneath a manufactured home.  The
home shifted off the jack stands and fell.  Employee #1 was caught between the
structure and the ground.  He was killed by crushing injuries to his torso,
neck, and head.  Employee #2 was hospitalized for treatment of unspecified
injuries.
At 7:15 a.m. on February 28, 2020, an employee was adjusting the single and
double line brakes of an overhead gantry crane while standing on the trolley
platform of the crane.  The employee told his coworker to test the brakes and
the trolley platform moved.  The employee was hit on his left side by a metal
ceiling beam from the building and fell into the rotating lines, crushing him.
The employee was killed.
At 9:15 a.m. on September 19, 2019, an employee was mixing plaster/cement
material in the mixer. The hose line had a blockage. It blew and sprayed the
employee with cement and foreign bodies. Plaster/cement and foreign bodies
entered the employee's eyes. He was wearing standard construction safety glasses
instead of goggles. The employee was hospitalized.
At 6:00 p.m. on March 12, 2020, an employee was unchaining a load to remove from
the trailer.  The employee stepped back off of the trailer and fell to the
ground (22 inches).  The employee broke his hip and was hospitalized.
At 8:00 a.m. on March 12, 2020, Employee #1, employed by a construction company,
was working at a multiemployer construction project along a two lane road.  He
was engaged in flagging operations within the work zone when an oncoming
automobile struck him.  Emergency services transported Employee #1 to the
hospital, where he died that day from traumatic head injuries.
At 6:20 p.m. on September 30, 2019, an employee was working at a facility which
performed the industrial washing of reusable plastic containers used for
packaging fruits and vegetables. The employee worked in the wet area on a
production line conveyor and his job duties involved removing stickers from the
bins.  After the containers exit the washing portion of the line, they drop onto
conveyor lines into the area where the employee was tasked with removing
stickers from the crates before collapsing them and stacking them onto pallets.
The employee was working in the area between two conveyor lines to access where
the containers entered from the washing area. The conveyor system consisted of a
plastic chain on each metal edge of the conveyor, with a shaft with four
sprockets connected to a small chain drive immediately after a 90 degree bend in
the conveyor. At the time of the incident, the shaft was protruding out from the
conveyor by approximately four to five inches. The employee's baggy high
visibility short sleeve shirt became caught in the shaft, as well as his fingers
within his latex dipped cotton gloves. The employee sustained an amputation of
the fourth and fifth fingertips of his left hand and was transported to the
regional medical center for treatment without hospitalization.

right hand off of the switch, the hydraulic lift moved slightly before
completely coming to a full stop. The employee had his left hand in the way and

hospitalized for more than 24 hours and surgery was performed on his hand. The

At 4:10 p.m. on September 18, 2019, an employee was pulling a tarp over some
trash that was on a trailer when his head came into contact with a sagging

to his body from burning trash.
On February 25, 2019, an employee was talking on the phone distracted when he
fell nearly 5 feet off a ramp onto the concrete floor. He received multiple
fractures to his collarbone and ribs and required medical treatment. The
employee was not hospitalized.
At 5:30 p.m. on September 25, 2019, an employee who worked as a Teacher for a
general medical and surgical hospital was riding a company owned shuttle bus
from the hospital building to the company parking lot to retrieve her car. The
employee slipped on the steps while exiting the shuttle bus and fell to the
ground. The employee was admitted to the hospital for surgery for a fractured
right hip.
At 4:45 a.m. on September 10, 2019, an employee was troubleshooting a
malfunction on the bottle tester machine when a coworker released the air
cylinder and the machine elevator self-corrected. The employee's hand was caught
between the top of the machine and the elevator. The employee was hospitalized
sustained a fractured left finger, torn ligaments, and a hyperextended knee and
was hospitalized.
At 7:30 a.m. on August 29, 2019, an employee was using a Husqvarna Model 372 XP
chain saw with a 24 inch blade to cut poplar trees with diameters as great as 28
inches into sections as long as 17 feet.  The employee was working on a sloped
hill with a 15 degree slant and had stepped over one tree to complete a cut that
he had made.  The employee was crushed by several logs when they began to roll
downhill and was killed.
At 1:00 p.m. on October 10, 2019, an employee, was placing a tote bag on a
dumping station in the production area. The employee was at the front of the
machine with his back facing pedestrian and vehicle traffic. The employee began
to walk backwards while observing the tote bag rise in the dumping station. A
coworker was picking up a palletized tote bag from the shelving unit and was
hauling it in front of his forklift. As the forklift turned the corner, the
coworker did not see the employee walking backwards. The right side corner of
the pallet struck the employee's leg. The employee suffered contusions on his
left leg and was treated without hospitalization.
At 10:00 a.m. on October 8, 2019, Employee #1 was removing a broken section of
concrete sidewalk from around a wrought iron fence.  As Employee #1 manually

At 12:45 p.m. on October 11, 2019, an employee was walking from the mill where
trucks load and unload feed and walked through a cloudy area where a front end
loader had delivered a load of Alfalfa.  The employee was struck in the head by
the bucket and was run over after falling to the ground.  The employee was
killed.
At 11:5 a.m. on October 16, 2019, an employee was performing exterior carpentry
at a residential construction project and was climbing on a ladder when it
listed to one side causing him to fall approximately eight feet with the ladder.
The employee was taken to the hospital, where he was treated and released with a
laceration to his head.
At 4:15 p.m. on October 15, 2019, an employee was unloading a truck when he was
struck by another truck that was backing up, pinning him against his truck.  The
employee was killed.
At 10:30 a.m. on September 30, 2019, an employee was performing maintenance on a
storage tank battery for oil and gas operations support. The employee was on a
crew which was working on a line which was not pressurizing properly. As the
employee was working on the line, the pop off valve relieved causing the
employee to be struck by released hydrogen sulfide. The employee fell off the
tank, rupturing his kidney and fracturing his left fibula and right hip. The
employee was hospitalized.
At approximately 1:00 p.m. on October 8, 2019, an employee was working for a
commercial lithographic printer. He operated a printing machine in the
converting department. He was directing the operator of a powered industrial
truck as he loaded a paper roll on a sheeter. The truck was a Clark Model
C5-S100 Type LP powered industrial truck, with serial number 685-0129-6655KCF.
It was equipped with a Cascade Corp. Model 60F-RC-03B roll clamp attachment,
with part number 2399353 and serial number 678702-P-79. The roll of paper was
some 62.25 or 62.5 inches (1.58 or 1.59 meters) in diameter. Several numbers
were given for the weight of the paper roll. The lowest weight was 1,500 pounds
(680 kg). The highest weight was 1,996 pounds (905 kg). The employer was
positioned in front of the paper roll on a walk located on the equipment,
providing guidance for the placement of the roll. The roll fell and rolled onto
the sheeter machine in an uncontrolled manner. It pushed the walkway and the
employee backward. The employee was caught between the sheeter machine and the
roll of paper. He suffered bruising and strains. He was taken by ambulance to a
hospital. He was hospitalized overnight. The employer did not contact Iowa OSHA
within twenty-four hours to report a workplace injury with hospitalization. The
employer's investigation report indicated that the employer was contacted on
October 9, 2019, by the employee when he returned home from the hospital the day
after the incident. On October 16, 2019, when OSHA appeared for an inspection,
the employer had not yet notified OSHA of the injury with hospitalization.
Problems with the clamp truck had been reported to the employer for over a year.
The truck was not taken out of service or repaired. During the summer an
employee was written up for dropping and damaging rolls. The employee noted in
his account that the clamp truck was faulty. He was told by management to work
with the available equipment.
At 8:00 a.m. on October 16, 2019, an employee was working on the paint line in
Section 1200 and entered into an area that was chained off with LOTO signs to
free a jammed pallet.  The employee was struck by a fiber concrete board that
was rejected by a Guidel Gantry Systems Robot and crushed between it and a stack
of other rejected boards, killing him.
At 9:00 a.m. on October 4, 2019, an employee working in a beverage manufacturing
company was picking products for shipping. The employee stepped off the
walker-rider forklift when it failed to stop and struck the employee on left
ankle. The employee incurred a deep laceration and fracture to his ankle and was
hospitalized.
At 11:30 a.m. on October 9, 2019, an employee who was a Manager for a cement
manufacturing facility was helping a coworker disassemble a cement Metal Type 3
hopper. The hopper shifted and fell over while the employee was working
underneath. The hopper fell on the employee causing head and chest injuries and
killed him.
At 4:00 p.m. on May 8, 2019, an employee was reaching into an energized WCB Ice
Cream Model #VL8 Versa Line Wrapper Machine with his right hand to lubricate a
clamp on the machine. The employee had his left hand resting on the machine
frame during this time. The machine would advance then stop for a moment, then
advance again. It was during the momentary stops that the employee would reach
in and spread the grease. At one point when the machine advanced, the employee's
left hand was caught by an exposed chain, which pulled his middle finger into a
sprocket nip point. The employee amputated his fingertip between the chain and
sprocket and required medical treatment.  The employee was not hospitalized.
At 5:00 p.m. on October 12, 2019, an employee was preparing food for an order
and cut his femoral artery with a chef's knife.  The employee was killed.
At 3:00 p.m. on October 9, 2019, an employee entered a trench with vertical
walls approximately 12 feet deep to take measurement of a sewer pipe's diameter.
The employee entered the excavation to obtain a measurement of the diameter of a
sewer pipe.  While inside the excavation, the south wall caved in.  The employee
was trapped against the north wall of the excavation to approximately chest
level.  The employee was trapped for approximately four hours while rescue
personnel attempted to free him.  The employee was transported and admitted to
St Francis Medical Center to treat fractured ribs.
At 8:30 p.m. on April 10, 2019, an employee, a garbage line sorter, was sorting
through the trash that came into the facility for anything that was recyclable
that may have been put into the trash such as plastics, glass, and metals while
wearing a hard hat and gloves. The employee was putting all metal objects into
Brute trash cans. As the employee's trash can became full with metal, she
dragged it to the end of the work platform and down the stairs to another work
platform where there were several dumpsters approximately 12 feet below where
the sorted material was dumped. The trash can was heavy so the employee asked a
coworker to assist her in dumping the metal out of the trash can. As the
equipment) to perform an earthwork construction operation.  Employee #1 moved
the hydraulic lines, at the base of the pile driving leads, so they were free to
move up and down with the hammer.  Afterwards, a wheel from the hydraulic gate
arm, assembly approximately 70 feet up the 2:1 leads, came off the bolt and
needle bearing assembly and struck Employee #1 in the head.  Employee #1 then
sustained head trauma and was killed.
At 10:53 a.m. on September 25, 2019, Employee #1, Employee #2 and Employee #3
were excavating a dirt roadway median, on a active two-lane roadway, during a
highway construction project.  A passing driver, of a 2013 Dodge Avenger, then
intruded into the roadway's median (worksite area), striking the three employees
working (on foot).  Afterward, the vehicle then collided with the front and
bucket of a mini excavator and finally stopped.    Employee #1 and Employee #2
were propelled into the air and landed in a westbound lane, on the roadway.
Employee #1 sustained blunt impact injuries and died.  Employee #2 received
emergency transport, was hospitalized and suffered two fractures of the left
leg, ligament damage to the right leg and head/scalp lacerations.  Employee #3
was grazed by the vehicle's side, fell onto the median, and suffered back and
wrist strain injuries and a torn meniscus in his right knee.
At 7:30 a.m. on September 10, 2019, a temporary employee was operating a grommet
machine to pierce grommets on the edges of banners for hanging purposes. The
employee was operating the machine by foot pedal when his hand got caught in the
point of operation. The machine was equipped with inadequate guarding. The
employee was hospitalized to treat an amputation of his right index fingertip.
At 6:45 a.m. on October 1, 2019, an employee was operating a magnetic drill
machine at a prefabricated metal building manufacturing facility. The employee's
left hand was caught in the point of operation under the rotating bit of the
drill machine.  The employee incurred a partial amputation of his left ring
finger, fractured his left pinky finger, and was hospitalized.
At 7:00 a.m. on May 23, 2019, an employee was cutting sections of extruded,
formed aluminum bar with a DeWalt Chop Saw, model Number D28715. While cutting a
section of bar, the chop saw jerked up the work piece suddenly. The employee's
left ring and index fingers were in the end of the extruded aluminum bar and
were injured when the work piece suddenly jerked up. The employee was
hospitalized to treat an amputation of the left ring fingertip and an injury of
the tip of the middle finger.
At 1:30 p.m. on September 12, 2019, an employee was cutting a wire at a
residential site to install a new cable drop. While working from a seven-foot
extension ladder, the employee came into contact with an unprotected 120-volt
electrical drop connection as he attempted to belt off to a service pole and was
shocked.  As a result, the employee fell and fractured his right arm.  The
employee was hospitalized.
At 1:15 p.m. on April 23, 2019, Employee #1, employed by a roofing company, was
engaged in roofing work at the site of a new one-story residential structure.
While walking on the roof, he stepped on a defective tile.  The tile broke, and
the employee fell from the roof, a fall height of 10 to 11 feet.  He was
transported to the hospital and admitted for treatment of a spinal injury.
At 11:30 a.m. on September 24, 2019, an employee was walking from the computer
lab to the school office that was located across the road and stepped up onto
the 6 inch curb.  The employee tripped on the edge of it and fell to the ground,
sustaining a subdural hematoma.  The employee was transported by EMS to the UCI
Medical Center and was given a high dosing of blood thinners.  The employee died
on October 7, 2019.
At 11:00 a.m. on May 3, 2019, an employee stood at the base of a water well to
readjust a bull tong that was wrapped around a twelve-inch well column pipe. The
bull tong was simultaneously being pulled by a chain attached to the hydraulic
ram of a fifty-ton pump hoist truck. As tension was applied, the chain of a
chain tong broke, swung down, and struck the employee's leg. The employee was
taken to the hospital and admitted to treat a compound fracture of the left
lower leg.
At 4:20 p.m. on September 28, 2019, an employee was painting the trim on the
exterior of a new addition to a single residential home when the Werner Aluminum
6-foot step ladder she was standing on moved causing her to lose balance and
fall. When the employee fell, her right leg slipped through the ladder and was
trapped causing her leg to break during the fall. The accident occurred because
the ladder was placed on uneven dirt ground. The employee suffered fractures to
her lower and upper leg that required surgery and hospitalization.
At 8:15 p.m. on October 6, 2019, Employee #1, the owner of a restaurant, noticed
an odor and smoke coming from an electrical vault. The patrons were cleared from
the restaurant, the patio area perimeter was secured, and the fire department
was contacted.  After the firefighters arrived, Employee #1 and a coworker led
the firefighters to the patio towards the vault.  The transformer vault
exploded, splashing the employee, coworker, and two firefighters with oil,
burning them. Employee #1 suffered second and third degree burns on 42 percent
of his body and was hospitalized. The coworker and the firefighters suffered
minor injuries.

the stuffing horns from Poly-Clip 3430 stuffing horns, preparing to change a

horn when the machine came on, causing the slicer/clipper to engage and
amputated the employee's left pinky finger. The employee was hospitalized for
these injuries.

were toned out to respond to a medical call. On the way to the call, they

At 3:30 p.m. on October 6, 2019, Employee #1 was standing on Cargo Hold Hatch 2,

At 1:30 p.m. on September 6, 2019, an employee was hospitalized to treat heat
stress after complaining about heat cramps.
At 12:15 p.m. on June 18, 2019, an employee was moving a safe using hand truck
when the truck struck debris on floor resulting in the safe and hand truck to
suddenly fall forward. The safe struck the employee on his left thigh which

At 10:00 a.m. on October 5, 2019, Employee #1 lifted a motor vehicle, using an
excavator equipped with a clamp, to remove the catalytic converter. As the
employee worked underneath of the vehicle while it was suspended, the vehicle
slipped out of the excavator clamp and crushed the employee between the car and

At 11:30 a.m. on October 4, 2019, an employee working in an elderly home was
cleaning a drain underneath a garbage disposal. The employee had mixed bleach

treatment.
At 2:08 p.m. on September 1, 2019, two employees were standing behind the turn 1
concrete barrier wall of a racetrack overseeing the "Tiger Model" class

track after having come off the track for repairs during the race. Employee #2
was positioned to be able to see the race track to look for debris and notify

the concluding last laps, when the race cars approached turn 1. Three cars
approached turn 1 side by side and began to collide just prior to entering the
turn. The outside racecar was forced into the straight stretch barrier wall. The
employee was hospitalized for treatment of lacerations to their right thigh and
arm.
At 4:00 a.m. on September 23, 2019, an employee was working behind the store
counter when a masked assailant entered the store and demanded money.  The
employee gave the assailant the money and was shot several times in the abdomen,
chest, and head.  The employee was killed.
At 1:05 a.m. on September 20, 2019, an employee was running off an unusable
portion of the fiberglass line.  During this process, the line became caught in

At 12:45 p.m. on September 14, 2019, an employee was retrieving a tire from the
third tier of a 3-tier racking system when he climbed up to the second level,
stepped onto another tire which slid off the shelf and caused him to fall. The
employee fell approximately 6 feet to the concrete floor and suffered fractures

At 12:45 p.m. on September 16, 2019, an employee was loading a decoiler machine
with a roll at a sheet metal work manufacturing facility. The 705 lb steel coil
roll was lifted with a wire mesh sling suspended on the forks of a forklift.
When the load shifted, the coil struck the employee and caused him to fracture
his ankle. The employee was hospitalized.
