gate, the gin pole failed striking the employee in the side of his head
rendering him unconscious. Employee died during transport to the hospital.
At 11:55 p.m. on December 23, 2019, an employee working for a wire manufacturer
was resetting a mechanical power press for a different operation. The press was
energized and not locked out during the set up process. The employee caught his
left hand in the press die when the machine cycled. The employee crushed his
index and middle fingers and required medical treatment without hospitalization.
At 8:27 a.m. on February 9, 2020, an employee was operating a tortilla making
machine when the wire that cuts the thickness of the tortillas broke. The
employee was trying to reinstall the wire with the machine operating when his
hand got caught in the drive gears. The employee was hospitalized to treat a
fractured thumb and had to have reconstructive surgery on the portion of the
hand between the thumb and index finger.
At 7:00 a.m. on February 21, 2020, two maintenance employees were
troubleshooting a material handling lift because it was malfunctioning.  They
placed blocks under the hydraulic lift for troubleshooting.  After
troubleshooting the hydraulic system, the employees were in the process of
removing the blocks from the hydraulic lift, when one of the employees placed
his hands on the lift.  One employee was operating the controls, and one
employee was to remove the blocks.  The employee operating the manual controls
told the other employee he was activating the lift and instructed the other
employee to remove the blocks.  The employee placed his hands on the lift, and
the lift raised up a couple inches and crushed the employee's fingers between
the lift and metal frame. The employee amputated his fingers and was
hospitalized.
At 8:15 a.m. on September 30, 2019, an employee and a coworker were dismantling
a metal scaffold at a new construction of a three-story house. The employee was
passing wooden planks to the coworker from the first level of the scaffold when
he fell. The employee was hospitalized to treat a fractured left cheek, nose,
pelvis, and wrists.
At 8:45 a.m. on February 7, 2020, Employee #1 was operating an off-road dump
truck for the removal of topsoil for a new 51-acre subdivision. After Employee
#1 dumped a load and was traveling the snow-covered path back to the excavator,
the dump truck's front tire fell into a test hole dug by a previous contractor
which stopped the dump truck abruptly. Employee #1 struck the side window of the
cab and steering wheel, resulting in fractured ribs, lacerations, a punctured
lung, and spleen damage.  The employee was hospitalized.
At 8:06 a.m. on September 14, 2019, an employee was descending a wooden stairway
from a roof of a building, holding onto his tools in his right hand and holding
onto a rail with his left hand. When he reached the next floor, the stairs
wooden tread gave way, and he fell 10 feet to a landing below. The employee
sustained a compound fracture to his right foot/ankle and was hospitalized.
At 7:35 a.m. on February 21, 2020, an employee was stepping over conduit, while
walking on a locked-out waste material vibrating conveyor. The employee slipped
while stepping over conduit and fell backwards.  The employee put his hands and
arms out to catch himself, and his right hand was caught in the unguarded moving
chain and sprocket of the adjacent transfer line conveyor chain and sprocket
drive belt for the roller conveyor. The employee suffered a right hand fingertip
partial amputation and was hospitalized.
At 9:00 a.m. on February 19, 2020, an employee, working for an electrical
company, stepped onto a catwalk platform and was struck on the head when bending
over. The employee's feet became stuck on the catwalk and the employee fell
approximately 7 feet 11 inches into a trench excavation near the platform. The
employee was hospitalized and treated for a fractured right arm and hip.
At 5:00 p.m. on January 9, 2020, the pipe lining crew was using a hot water
system to inflate a liner inside a pipe. Hot water and 6.5 pounds of pressure
were added to invert the tubes inside the pipes. An employee was standing next
to the tube. The tube burst at the seam, spraying hot water on the employee. The
tube was brand new. The employee suffered second and third degree burns to the
right side of his body. The employee was hospitalized.
At 5:30 a.m. on February 22, 2020, an employee was cleaning a stock room when he
was shot in the chest by a robber.  The employee was killed.
At 7:50 a.m. on February 18, 2020, an employee was working at a sawmill. He was
a laborer. He was at the sawmill's edger operator station, at the end of the
green chain line where employees stack lumber. He was operating a McDonough
edger. He was feeding boards and cants from the head saw and resaw into the
edger. The resaw was a model number WPRS-ECD West Plains Resaw Systems, Inc.
resaw, with serial number 1006. He was reaching for a board over a rotating
starting to back up. The food truck ran over the employee. Paramedics were
called, and the employee was airlifted and transported to a local hospital. The
employee was hospitalized to treat multiple fractures.
At approximately 7:06 p.m. on March 14, 2018, an employee part of the sanitation
team was working at a Tamale Department. The employee was cleaning an assembly
conveyor at the time of the incident with a water hose and lifted the conveyor
part while the machine was running. The employee got her right ring finger
caught by a part of the machine during cleaning operations. The employee
suffered right ring finger burn/abrasion.  The employee was hospitalized for
these injuries.
At 8:00 a.m. on August 8, 2019, an employee was moving a casting, approximately
500 pounds, with an overhead crane and lifting device. The casting fell from the
lifting device onto the employee's foot/leg. The employee was hospitalized for a
broken foot/ankle/leg.
At 1:00 p.m. on August 27, 2019, an employee was finishing cement on a hot,
humid day when he was overcome with heat exhaustion.
At approximately 2:30 p.m. on January 31, 2020, Four employees (Employee #1 and
three coworkers) were engaged in manual felling of two oak trees from the work
site in North Falmouth, Massachusetts.    Coworker # 3 was working from a
trailer mounted aerial lift removing the branches from the trees.  Coworker #2
was on the ground cutting the branches into smaller pieces and assisting
Employee #1 in moving the branches to the chipper.  Coworker #3, who was the
crew manager, was working in the work zone while Coworker#1 was responsible for
felling the trunk.   As Coworker #1 was preparing to fell the trunk, Employee #1
and Coworker #3 were within the work zone.  Employee #1 was feeding branches
into the chipper and Coworker #3 was standing approximately three to four (3-4)
feet behind Employee #1 as he prepared to fell the trunk.  Employee #1 and
Coworker #2 were closer than twice the height of the trunk being felled as
required by ANSI Z133-2017.  The trunk being felled was approximately sixteen
(16) feet in length and had a diameter of approximately sixteen (16) inches.  As
the trunk fell, it landed on a second branch that was approximately eight (8)
inches in diameter and approximately eight (8) feet in length.  When the trunk
landed on the branch, it catapulted the branch across the worksite, striking
Employee #1 in the forehead and was approximately twenty-six (26) feet away from
the base of the trunk.  None of the employees was wearing protective helmets.
Employee #1 was struck in the forehead causing significant head trauma with a
skull fracture, resulting in being killed.
At 11:30 a.m. on October 26, 2019, an employee was operating standup forklift
when he collided with a storage rack. The employee's foot was crushed between
the lower portion of forklift he was operating and the lower frame guard of rack
he struck. The employee was hospitalized to treat a fracture and laceration to
his left foot.
At 11:20 a.m. on September 20, 2019, an employee working for a confectionary
manufacturer stated that he had been passing boxes of product to a coworker.
When the employee was heading back to get the next box, he stepped on a carton
and fell off the 6-foot platform. The employee reported muscle tightness due to
the fall. The employee was not using any fall protection system. The employee
were hospitalized and treated for their injuries.
At 7:30 a.m. on January 31, 2020, an employee was utilizing the top half of an
extension ladder to access a wood shelving system.  The bottom of the ladder
slid out and the employee fell approximately 10 feet to the concrete floor. The
employee sustained a right crushed elbow, right ulna fracture, left elbow
displacement and fracture, left hip contusion, and right shoulder pain.  The
employee was hospitalized and had surgery to repair the right ulna fracture and
replace the right elbow.
At 5:00 a.m. on February 3, 2020, an employee working for an appliance
manufacturer was removing a metal slug from Press 209. The employee was on the
back scott line of the fabrication process when she attempted to clear the
debris from the machine. The employee reached into the die when the ram came
down on her forearm. She fractured her arm in two places and required
hospitalization.
At 8:00 a.m.  on February 14, 2020,  a Local Emphasis Program Inspection was
conducted.
At 11:15 a.m. on February 5, 2020, an employee working as an electrician for a
foundry coke producer was chasing a wire. The employee lost his balance and his
hand struck a mechanical motor. The employee amputated his left middle and ring
fingers and required hospitalization.
At 5:30 a.m. on January 27, 2020, an employee was attempting to place a clevis
pin on a section of fiberglass cooling tower wall when group of 30 foot long
fiberglass sections fell onto him.  The employee was hospitalized to treat a
fractured right.
At 10:10 p.m. on February 1, 2020, Employee #1 was assisting a coworker,
grilling brats on two 12-inch charcoal camping grills in the maintenance shop.
The coworker attempted to ignite charcoal in one of the grills by using
denatured alcohol as a lighter fluid.  The denatured alcohol ignited while being
poured, and created a large ball of fire that burned the left arm and face of
Employee #1.  Employee #1 was transferred to Memorial Medical Center in
Springfield, IL and admitted for treatment of second degree burns to the face
and left arm.
At 8:00 a.m. on February 14, 2020, a Local Emphasis Inspection Safety Inspection
was conducted.
At 2:30 p.m. on February 11, 2020, an employee working as a machine operator for
a wooden pallet manufacturer was pushing a piece of plywood into a saw. The
employee pushed start button when the hold down pinched his finger and the saw
blade started to travel. The employee amputated his finger and required medical
treatment without hospitalization.
At 9:30 a.m. on September 14, 2019, an employee was cleaning up a construction
site.  The employee and two coworkers moved a big piece of broken asphalt.  As
the employee started loading a bucket by lifting the first layer of asphalt, the
second layer lifted up as well.  The employee's index finger was pinched,
resulting in amputation.  The employee was treated without hospitalization.
At 11:30 a.m. on August 21, 2019, an employee removed the cover of an HVAC unit
before the belt and pulley stopped rotating. The employee's finger became caught
in the nip point and received a fingertip amputation. The employee was taken to
the hospital for treatment without hospitalization.
At 4:00 p.m. on January 10, 2020, an employee was performing demolition work,
removing burnt trusses from a fire-damaged garage. The employee was standing on
the eve overhang of the roof while pulling a piece of wood when the wood hit him
on the leg and caused him to lose his balance. The employee fell approximately
16 feet to the concrete driveway. The employee was hospitalized to treat a
fractured pelvis.
At 11:00 a.m. on October 4, 2019, an employee was walking under a power line
while carrying a 28 foot metal pole in a upright position. The metal pole struck
one of the wires attached to the power line, shocking the employee.  The
employee was transported to the hospital via air ambulance to be treated for
third degree burns on his torso and lower extremities.
At 4:00 p.m. on February 5, 2020, an employee working as a welder for a rolled
steel manufacturer was standing to the side of an aisle. A coworker operating a
forklift came around the corner with an empty scrap box on the forks. The empty
scrap box hit an empty scrap box on the floor causing it to move 6 to 12 inches
and striking the employee and pinning the employee between the box and a
guardrail. The employee broke his pelvis and was hospitalized.
At 3:30 p.m. on February 13, 2020, an employee was climbing on the end bracing
of a scaffold while waiting for a concrete truck. At some point, either
ascending or descending the scaffold (no witnesses were present), the employee
fell approximately eighteen feet and was killed due to blunt force trauma to the
head.
At 12:00 p.m. on February 7, 2020, Employee #1 was standing on scaffolding using
the hose from a concrete pump truck to fill concrete forms. An air pocket
developed within the formwork that caused the concrete to exert pressure outward
which caused the hose to strike Employee #1's face. Employee #1 fell backwards
off the scaffolding to the ground 6 feet below. Employee #1 suffered fractures
of both elbows, fracture of left cheek, fracture of left wrist, fractured neck,
and lacerations to the face and lip and was hospitalized.
At 12:44 p.m. on December 20, 2019, an owner and two employees of a marine
construction company were constructing a seawall on a residential property.  The
owner was operating a Kubota KX057-4R1 Mini Excavator with a Stanley HSX6
Vibratory Plate Compactor unit attached to the boom. The compactor was being
utilized to drive pressure treated 2-inch by 10-inch by 12-foot tongue and
groove sheet piling into the soil to form the vertical members of the seawall.
After the excavator completed driving a sheet piling into the soil, the owner
elevated the boom with vibratory compactor unit to allow the employees to
prepare and place the next sheet piling to be driven into place. As the employee
stepped underneath the vibratory compactor implement, the unit detached from the
boom and fell on him. The employee was struck on the left shoulder and left
side, was forced to the ground, and the compactor unit landed on his chest
pinning him. The employee was transported to a nearby trauma center and was
admitted for treatment.
At 1:40 a.m. on January 15, 2020, an employee was directing Coworker #1 who was
operating an overhead crane lowering the 29 foot by 2 foot headache bar. The
employee was trying to reach a point on the crane hook while Coworker #2 was
directing the crane to lower the headache bar more.  This created slack in the
crane chains making the headache bar unstable and causing it to fall over onto
the employee. The employee incurred a fractured ankle and was hospitalized.
At 11:15 a.m. on January 21, 2020, an employee was using a cloth to clean under
an oven when his bare finger contacted a sharp edge. The employee lacerated his
finger and broke his fingernail, requiring medical treatment without
hospitalization.
At 10:45 p.m. on January 15, 2020, an employee was sitting on a concrete pad on
a dock listening to music on his phone. The employee dropped his phone over the
dock rub rail as a switch truck was backing into the dock. When the employee
reached over the rub bar he was struck by the Interstate Commerce Commission
(ICC) bar located on the trailer of the switch truck. The employee fractured his
ribs and lacerated a kidney, requiring hospitalization.
At 8:00 a.m. on January 9, 2020, an employee was tasked to look for a route to
install plumbing lines for a bathroom on the second floor.  The area itself was
a room with a hallway in between, leading to another open area, and to one side
was a frame wall with no drywall up, and the other side was a framed elevator
shaft with no drywall up and no railings on part of the wall.  The lighting
itself was very poor, only about 0.02-0.06 fc.  The employee was talking to a
coworker while looking up at the ceiling and walking backwards and, in the
process, he walked through the opening in the wall to the elevator shaft and
fell to the ground, approximately 5 feet, hitting beams that were inside the
shaft on the way down.  The employee sustained serious injuries to his leg and
hip and was hospitalized.
At 8:00 p.m. on January 16, 2020, Employee #1 and Employee #2 were riding in the
back of a flatbed truck moving metal frame and highway caution signs. Two
coworkers rode in the inside of the truck cab and were driving. While the truck
was moving, one of the highway caution signs flew up and struck Employee #1 and
Employee #2. Employee #1 fell from the moving truck and struck his head on the
highway road, resulting in fractures to his head and was killed.  No information
was provided in the original narrative about the injuries to Employee #2.
At 6:20 a.m. on January 7, 2020, an employee was working near a conveyor when
his hand got caught in the unguarded chain and sprocket. The employee suffered a
left ring finger amputation and was treated without hospitalization.
At 7:50 a.m. on December 31, 2019, an employee, a machinist, was operating the
only CNC Lathe the company owns.  The employee worked for a fabricator of metal
components for gas burning products.  The employee stated he had just finished
machining one of the parts, and had his left hand in the air, not paying
attention, with the guard door open and lathe spindle spinning. His left hand
had a glove on it, and the spinning spindle caught the glove and pulled his left
hand into the rotating spindle and cutter blades, resulting in an amputation of
his left index finger.  The employee was treated without hospitalization.  One
of the contributing factors was the guard door for the cutter blades slides left
to right.  With the guard door in the far-left position, the cutter blades are
completely enclosed but with the guard door in the far-right position, the
cutter blades are completely exposed.  The accident happened because there is
nothing to stop the rotating cutter blades when the guard door is fully opened
to the right.  One violation is an accident-related citation for the point of
operation not being guarded.
At 12:30 p.m. on January 16, 2020, an employee was accessing an upper part of a
roof using a Werner portable fiberglass extension ladder (Model: D6332-2) on a
commercial construction site while carrying a 5-gallon bucket with roofing
materials. The employee received training on the safe use of portable extension
ladders and inspected the ladder prior to use. The temperature was 0 degrees
Fahrenheit, no winds, fair visibility, and snow was present on the rooftop
level. The employee slipped and fell approximately 16 feet 6 inches and suffered
a fractured sternum, fractured ribs, fractured vertebrae, a punctured lung, and
a concussion. The employee was hospitalized in the intensive care unit for 8
days and required rehab for treatment of their injuries.
At 11:30 a.m. on January 10, 2020, an employee was removing a metal piece from a
plasma burner with a magnet connected to a crane. The piece got stuck and the
employee tried to dislodge it with his hand. The employee caught his hand
between the piece and the slats on the burner, causing him to amputate his
finger and require medical treatment without hospitalization.
At 11:30 p.m. on January 15, 2020, an employee was opening the steam vent on a
fractionator when the condensate burped out of the vent. The employee incurred
second degree burns on his back and shoulders, requiring hospitalization.
At 2:00 a.m. on November 16, 2019, Employee #1 was milking cows in the milking
barn. Employee # 1 tried to free a cow, which had gotten stuck in the milking
stall, by placing both of his hands on the cow's head and pushing it back. The
cow raised its head and crushed the employee's left pinky against the top metal
rail of the milking machine structure. Employee #1 was hospitalized to treat a
crush injury to his left fourth finger.
At 1:30 p.m. on January 10, 2020, an employee was seen eating lunch in the
manufacturing workplace. Around 4:00 p.m. on the same day, coworkers found the
employee unconscious on the floor of the workplace between two counters.  The
coworkers called emergency services and the employee was pronounced dead on the
scene by the local Fire Department. The Los Angeles County Coroner retrieved the
hospitalized for treatment.
At approximately 10:00 a.m. on January 23, 2020, an employee was exiting an
office to return to her office.  While walking back, the employee struck a chair
with her foot/knee and suffered a same level fall.  The fall resulted in a
fractured hip.
At 5:03 p.m. on November 2019, an employee working as a retail Salesclerk for a
seasonal clothing and decorations store was attempting to retrieve material from
a shelf using an A-frame stepladder. A customer threw an object which struck the
drop ceiling which caused a metal frame bar to drop from the ceiling. This
distracted the employee and caused him to fall from the ladder to the concrete
floor. The employee sustained a concussion and contusions to his head, neck,
back and stomach and was hospitalized.
At 3:00 p.m. on January 29, 2020, an employee working as a laborer for a tree
care company was trimming a gumbo limbo tree. The employee was strapped
approximately 18 to 20 feet up in the tree when the tree broke near the base.
Although safety precautions were in place the employee was not wearing a helmet.
The employee struck his head on the ground and was transported to the hospital
possibly needing stitches. Upon review at the hospital, the medical provider
determined he may need surgery for a cranial fracture. He was transferred to a
trauma center, where a CAT scan caused the medical providers to question if
surgery was needed. The employee was admitted to the hospital for observation
due to head trauma including a cranial fracture.
At 2:30 p.m. on January 31, 2020, an employee was moving the JLG lift. It
slipped off of the levee.  The employee sustained multiple fractures to the leg
and was hospitalized.
At 9:30 a.m. on January 31, 2020, an employee was working in the storage yard,
marking product size, type, etc.  The employee was struck by falling bundles of
steel box channel (48 feet by 4 inches by 10 inches, 1,564 pounds)  that
collapsed as he was stepping onto them to mark them. The bundles fell off the
front of the dunnage that they had been placed on by another employee. The
following are the factors that would have prevented the accident: proper and
secure stacking of the steel bundles to prevent them from falling. The employee
suffered multiple fractures to his leg, foot, heel, and ankle.  The employee was
transported to Riverside Community Hospital, where he was hospitalized for three
days.   Prior to and during the course of the Investigation, including, but not
limited to February 5, 2020, the employer failed to ensure that stacked material
(2 bundles of steel tube, 10x4x.375, 48 ft in length, approx. 2000 lbs) was
secured in a way to prevent it from tipping, falling, collapsing, rolling, or
spreading. As a result, on or about January 31, 2020, an employee fell from the
bundle of steel that collapsed beneath him, trapping his leg, causing serious
injuries. steel box channel (48 feet by 4 inches by 10 inches, 1564 lbs)
At 11:00 a.m. on January 31, 2019, Employee #1, a machine operator, was running
the Hayssen packaging machine in the production bean room, when the machine
stopped bagging correctly.  Employee #1 attempted to unjam the machine by
reaching into the cutting jaws of the machine, while the machine was still
running, and received an amputation of the left index fingertip.  The employee
was treated without hospitalization.
At 3:00 p.m. on February 5, 2020, Employee #1 was working from a 6-foot step
ladder attaching a plywood strip for window installation. Employee #1 fell off
the ladder during descent and fell to the ground. Employee #1 suffered a skull
fracture and was hospitalized.
At 11:00 a.m. on August 15, 2019, an employee directed concrete flowing down an
"elephant trunk" from a plastic hopper situated on the raised forks of a
complete and the tool-changer arm to strike the employee in the chest. There was
one eyewitness to the incident.
At 12:05 p.m. on February 25, 2020, an employee was injured when his finger got
caught in a surface grinder wheel.  The employee was hospitalized.
At 8:39 a.m. on February 25, 2020, an employee was cutting chicken wings using a
wing saw. A coworker came up to the employee and tapped him on the shoulder,
causing him to look away from his work. The employee was distracted, and his
right thumb came into contact with the blade of the wing saw. The employee's
right thumb was partially amputated and was treated without hospitalization.
On December 10, 2019, an employee was laying plywood to be nailed by his
coworker to a panelized frame with a nail gun. As the employee moved towards his
coworker, the employee put his arm towards his coworker and the coworker turned
towards him.  The coworker depressed the trigger of the nail gun, shooting a
nail into the employee's wrist.  The employee was impaled by the nail and
hospitalized.
At 9:40 a.m. on March 4, 2020, an employee was driving a log truck, when he
hospitalized.
started coughing and choking, then passed out. The loaded truck crossed two
lanes of traffic, ran off the road and overturned on to its side. The employee
hospitalized.
was transported to Mercy Medical in Roseburg Oregon and was admitted overnight
for observation.  The employee sustained broken ribs and a collapsed lung.
At 2:00 p.m. on November 27, 2019, while attempting to charge the battery on a
John Deere 300 B, the tractor started and jumped forward and ran over an
employee.  The employee had been standing on the left side of the tractor,
reached over to try to start the tractor, bumped the shifter (located on the
left side) into gear, causing the tractor to run the employee over.  The
employee's top 10 ribs and scapula were fractured. The employee was
hospitalized.
At 4:30 p.m. on March 5, 2020, an employee was standing in a trench next to the
bucket of an excavator unhooking a sling while the operator was moving the
backhoe boom.  The excavator control lever was, then, activated causing the
bucket to move laterally that crushed the employee between the wall of the
trench and the bucket.  The employee was killed from injuries sustained from a
crushed chest.
At 11:00 a.m. on September 12, 2019, an employee was walking between the
skylights, across the roof, when he fell through one of the skylights to the
concrete working surface below and suffered serious injuries.  The employee was
hospitalized.  Factors contributing to the accident was that the employees
working and walking within 6 feet of the skylights were not protected from
falling through the skylights with any of the following methods: (1) Skylight
screens installed above the skylights. (2) Skylight screens installed below the
skylights. (3) Guardrails. (4) The use of a personal fall protection systems.
(5) Covers. (6) Skylight nets. (7) No fall protection plan as prescribed in
Section 1671.1 of the Construction Safety Orders
At 3:15 p.m. on January 11, 2020, Employee #1, employed by a construction
company, and a coworker, the company owner, were working on the construction of
a new residence.  Employee #1 was installing trusses when he fell backwards,
struck his head, and lost consciousness.  The company owner performed CPR while
waiting for emergency services to arrive.  The employee was transported by air
to the hospital and admitted to the intensive care unit.  He died the following
day, January 12, 2020, at approximately 2:00 p.m.
At 3:30 p.m. on March 2, 2020, an employee working as a maintenance technician
for a linen supply company was checking with a coworker (also maintenance) to
see if he needed assistance on a job. The employee was repairing a problem with
a bag lift. He pulled the rope on the bag, opened the control panel of the lift
and "bumped" the lift manually with a connector until the bars aligned. The
employee went to the side of the lift and reached over a cart to toggle the
limit switch. At this time, the lift came down pinning the employee between the
bar and the cart. The employee broke six ribs and punctured a lung, requiring
hospitalization.
At 9:00 a.m. on February 22, 2020, an employee was operating a pipe crimper and
van that crushed the employee.  The employee was killed after suffering
fractures to his head and back.
At 7:20 a.m. on March 15, 2020, an employee was removing bales of hay from an
elevated stack approximately 9-feet high when he lost his balance and fell. The
employee was hospitalized to treat fractures to all of the ribs on the left side
of his body.
At 2:50 p.m. on March 9, 2020, an employee working as a machine operator for a
plumbing and heating equipment supplier removed a doubled stacked pan from
Station #3, the Hold Punch Station. The employee then handed one of the pans to
a coworker to place onto Station #4, the Beading Station. The employee placed
the other pan on Station #3. The coworker hit the machine reset button causing
the hold punch machine to cycle while the employee was lining up the pan on
Station #3. The employee caught his left thumb between the punch hole die and
pan. The employee amputated his thumb tip and received medical treatment without
hospitalization.
At 10:00 a.m. on September 24, 2019, an employee was working at the private
residence of the employer who was constructing an addition to their home. The
employer was setting a double door with a light between the workshop and the
workspace in the building adjacent to the residence. The employee was using a
Rockwell International table saw, Model 34-761, to rip 1 inch by 1 inch wood
shims for setting the door. The saw had no guard, no anti-kickback device and no
spreader installed. The employee was not using a push stick but was using both
hands to feed the wood through the saw to rip the shims. The employee had made
approximately 10 cuts before a piece he was ripping kicked back causing his hand
to contact the rotating saw blade.  The employee suffered significant
lacerations to his left hand, requiring hospitalization for treatment that
lasted more than 24 hours.
At 11:45 a.m. on September 27, 2019, an employee who worked as a Master Service
Technician in an automotive service department was servicing a vehicle. The
employee was using a Hunter Scissor Lift Rack with swing air jacks for
alignments and a screw pole jack used to support the vehicle on the lift. The
employee had been working for the employer employer for approximately 1 month
and was scheduled to work 40 hours per week Monday through Friday. That morning
the employee had completed a brake job on another vehicle when a coworker (his
Supervisor) assigned him the alignment and tire rotation job that needed to be
completed by 2:00 p.m. The employee placed the vehicle on the Hunter Alignment
rack and lifted the vehicle approximately 5 to 6 feet from the ground. He then
picked the front end up with the swing air jacks then did the same with the rear
end of the vehicle for the purpose of rotating the tires. After the employee
completed the tire rotation he began to lower the vehicle off of the air jacks
so that he could complete the alignment. As he was trying to lower the vehicle
down it became unbalanced and shifted pinning the employee's head between the
scissor lift and the frame of the vehicle. The employee was transported to the
hospital, where he was admitted and underwent surgery for a fractured skull and
multiple facial lacerations.

infeed roller system.  Once the board was cut, the employee would take the

guard had adjustable guards which were not adjusted.  Each new set of boards
required the operator to cut 1-2 off to ensure a true square cut.  The employee
placed his hand in the outfeed section of the inadequately guarded outfeed
opening and was adjusting the board since the operator had pushed the boards too
far forward.  As the employee was pushing the board back, the machine operator
had activated the clamp, which was used to hold the boards in place.  A short

between the outfeed guard and saw blade was approximately 18 inches.  The
operator would have been positioned nearly directly in front of the saw blade.

At 8:45 a.m. on August 28, 2019, Employee #1 was working from a ladder at a

Model TS200LS bench saw. The ten inch bench saw blade was unguarded and rotating

boards when his right hand contacted the rotating blade. The employee's right
middle finger was amputated to the first knuckle, and he was hospitalized.
At 10:00 a.m. on October 1, 2019, Employee #1, a heavy equipment technician, was
doing machine/equipment maintenance. He was standing between a Caterpillar
Asphalt Vibratory Compactor (Roller) and another piece of heavy construction
equipment, testing the brakes. The brakes failed on the Roller, and it moved
forward. Employee #1 was crushed between the two pieces of machinery, and
killed.
At 11:30 a.m. on October 2, 2019, an employee was clearing a jam on a conveyor
belt while it was running when he was pulled into the rollers. The employee was
hospitalized to treat an amputation of his arm below the elbow.
At 8:25 p.m. on August 27, 2019, an employee was transporting a hot bag of soup

At 11:30 a.m. on October 7, 2019, Employee #1 was driving KLX Truck #427 to drop

attack.
At 9:56 a.m. on October 4, 2019, an employee was installing underground conduit
pipes for utility lines and was with his foreman cleaning the bottom of a 6-foot
trench using a shovel when one side of the wall collapsed and buried him up to
his chest.  The employee was hospitalized for treatment of fractured ribs.
At 5:30 p.m. on April 12, 2019, Employee #1 (cook) was retrieving chicken that
had finished cooking from a Henny Model PXE-100 Pressure Fryer. When Employee #1
raised the handle to open the fryer hot grease came flying out. Employee #1 and
Employee #2 (cook) who standing nearby assisting both sustained multiple burns
and were hospitalized.
At 6:45 a.m. on October 7, 2019, Employee #1 was track switching for a coworker,
who was operating a Rail King shuttle engine. The two employees were attempting
to separate loaded train cars from unloaded. After Employee #1 switched the
track lever, he signaled by hand to the coworker to start moving the train.
Employee #1 then realized that he did not set the soft brake on the last
railcar, and attempted to set the brake while the train was starting to move.
Employee #1 tripped on the track switch, causing him to fall onto the tracks,
where he was fatally struck by the train. Employee #1 was dragged approximately
260 feet underneath the train before it stopped. He sustained crushing injuries
and amputation of the left lower extremities, resulting in death. His body was
found by the coworker.
At 2:30 p.m. on October 2, 2019, an employee and a coworker were waiting inside
a windmill tower on the bottom level for cables to be dropped down to them. A
coworker approximately 200 feet above dropped a bolt that was used to connect
the wind tower sections together. The bolt struck the employee's hard hat. The
employee was hospitalized to treat a skull fracture.
At 11:15 a.m. on June 6, 2019, an employee was utilizing a fabricated, 1/4 inch
demolding tool to separate a fiberglass part from a mold. The employee was
applying air pressure to the mold to release a part however, due to excessive
pressure built up, the part released from the mold and ejected in the employee's
direction. The employee was struck in the head by the fiberglass part. The
employee was hospitalized to treat a skull fracture.
At 12:30 p.m. on October 4, 2019, Employee #1, #2, and #3 were assembling
sections of a galvanized steel metal framing for a party tent. A 20-foot section
of the galvanized steel metal framing for the tent made contact with overhead
electrical power lines, which subsequently energized the entire metal tent
frame. Employee #1 was electrocuted and killed. Employee #2 and #3 sustained a
non-fatal electric shock.
At 12:00 p.m. on October 7, 2019, Employee #1, the framing company owner

roofing truss members then collapsed onto Employee #1.  Employee #1 was then
fatally struck, crushed and killed.
At 3:00 p.m. on April 25, 2019, an employee was working at a hanger making

suffered a finger laceration.  The employee was treated but not hospitalized.
At 8:30 a.m. on January 11, 2019, an employee was unjamming a respirator on the
8 Head Auto Stapling Line when he caught his finger in the unguarded belt and
pulley. He amputated his left finger requiring medical treatment.  The employee
was not hospitalized.
On September 27, 2019, an employee was loading a trailer when he caught his hand
between the loaded pallet jack and a mobile cart. The employee amputated a
fingertip and required hospitalization.

from the roof into a trailer, the carport collapsed.  The employee jumped 8 feet

At 8:20 a.m. on September 18, 2019, an employee, a maintenance worker, was

The employee was struck by the forklift and the wheel ran over his ankle. The

At 10:30 a.m. on September 17, 2019, an employee was on the working level of a
scaffold, installing and leveling bricks with a brick trowel and level.  The
employee slipped from the scaffold, falling 22 feet 10 inches to the concrete
below.  The employee sustained multiple lower body fractures, requiring
hospitalization.
At 3:30 p.m. on September 18, 2019, an employee who works as a rigger for a
utilities contractor was installing water lines at a new construction site. The
employee collapsed from heat exhaustion and was hospitalized.
At 11:00 a.m. on September 12, 2019, an employee was dismantling a buck hoist.
The motor pack fell and crushed the employee. The employee was hospitalized to
treat several fractured ribs, as well as upper extremity injuries.
At 8:30 p.m. on September 18, 2019, an employee was replacing three fluorescent
light units with LED light units in the human resources office. The employee
turned lights off using two toggle switches but did not deenergize the light
units prior to conducting the work. While installing the second LED light unit,
the employee suffered an electric shock and fell off the ladder. The employee
was able to free himself from the electrical current but suffered second-degree
burns to his right hand, a labral tear, and a crushing injury to the right
shoulder, requiring hospitalization.
At 10:56 a.m. on September 6, 2019, an employee was operating a spring cap
machine trying to clear a jam. The employee placed her left ring finger in an
unguarded pinch point and fractured her fingertip, requiring hospitalization.

At 11:30 a.m. on September 20, 2019, an employee was moving skids with a Raymond
stand-up forklift.  The employee reversed the forklift into a steel rack,

hospitalized to treat fractured ribs and internal bleeding.
At 9:45 a.m. on August 24, 2019, an employee stood on a ladder inside a shoring
tower (Peri Multi-prop) to unhook rigging attached to the tower. After removing
the rigging, the employee signaled a crane operator to raise the rigging
equipment attached to the hook. While the hook began to lift, the rigging
snagged on a pin attached to the shoring tower and caused the tower to tip and
fall over. The employee also fell approximately seventeen feet when the ladder,
leaning against the inside of the tower also fell. The employee was hospitalized

At 1:45 p.m. on September 17, 2019, an employee was on a scissor lift,
installing an 8-inch 90-degree drainpipe to a ceiling.  The drainpipe slipped
from an attachment piece and the employee reached to grab the pipe.  The
employee fell out of the lift, approximately 12-feet to the ground level below.
The employee sustained multiple arm fractures, requiring hospitalization.
At 11:15 a.m. on March 18, 2019, an employee was labeling merchandise which
required opening boxes, retrieving products, affixing labels and returning them
to the boxes. A few boxes placed on the table fell to the other side where
employee was standing.  When the employee went around her table to retrieve the
boxes she tripped on a pallet and fell onto the concrete floor. She fractured
her hip and was hospitalized.
On June 11, 2019, Employee #1, a truck driver employed by a construction
company, had parked his 2008 Peterbilt semi-tractor and 2017 Kaufman detachable
gooseneck lowboy trailer on a sloping access road at a construction site.  He
was using a Caterpillar skid steer secured on top of the trailer platform to
raise the platform.  As Employee #1 stood between the tractor and the trailer,
the vehicle began to roll backward.  The tractor's rear wheels ran over Employee
#1, who was killed.  The subsequent investigation determined that the truck's
engine had been running; the parking brake had not been engaged; and the proper
number and sized wheel chocks had not been used while the vehicle was parked on
the incline.
At 12:00 p.m. on September 16, 2019, an employee was working with two coworkers
to install a wood framework on a two story residential home. The employee was
working from a truss when the truss collapsed and the employee fell nine and a
half feet, striking the second floor and then further fell an additional ten and
a half feet to the concrete floor of the first floor. The employee was killed by
unspecified injuries sustained in the fall.

dump millings into a single axle dump truck. The employee left the operator's
position in the skid steer to clean off the windshield and was standing at the
rear of the dump truck in the dump truck operators blind spot. The coworker
operating the dump truck began to move the dump truck in reverse without an
operational backup alarm. The employee was caught between the rear of the dump
truck and the front of the skid steer, where he sustained blunt force trauma to
the abdomen and was killed.
At 11:30 a.m. on September 25, 2019, an employee was climbing down a ladder
during siding repairs on a single family residence. The ladder slid out from
under the employee causing him to fall. The employee injured his hip and
required hospitalization.
At 6:04 p.m. on September 21, 2019, an employee was riding a bike making food
deliveries when he was struck by a truck.  The employee was knocked to the
street and struck his head on the ground, killing him.
At 3:45 p.m. on September 23, 2019, an employee was in the process of moving a
shoulder/road widening machine at the end of the workday. It is unknown if the
employee was ejected from or jumped from the machine due to a malfunction. The
employee was hospitalized to treat severe head trauma.
At 1:30 p.m. on September 18, 2019, an employee and two coworkers were changing

mill for support while the 1,500 PSI hydraulically-actuated hood guard was
closing. The employee's fingers got caught  in the pinch point between the band
mill's frame and the hood guard. The employee was hospitalized and his right
middle finger was amputated to the first knuckle and his right ring finger was
fractured.
At 11:15 p.m. on September 24, 2019, an employee was operating a concrete saw in

employee received medical treatment for amputations of the fleshy part of two
fingertips, but was not hospitalized.

operator for a manufacturer of wooden containers and pallets. He was operating a
Trio pallet disassembler to dismantle pallets. As he was cutting a pallet, his
glove became caught in the disassembler saw on the table. His right thumb was
amputated. He was treated without hospitalization.
At 12:00 a.m. on August 29, 2019, an employee was troubleshooting a Fryolator
deep fryer at a restaurant. The employee was unaware that the fryer's electrical
cord was damaged. When the employee touched the energized unit, she received an
electrical shock. The employee required medical treatment but was not
hospitalized.
At 1:00 p.m. on September 5, 2019, an employee was driving a Kenworth corn
silage truck to bring a load to the dairy when he took a right turn at a high
rate of speed and the vehicle rolled over onto the driver's side. The employee
was hospitalized to treat a fractured left arm.
At 1:10 p.m. on August 21, 2019, an employee was operating a John Deere 7130
Tractor with a Johnson MD Series Power Mulcher to rotor till the field's soil to
prepare it for planting.  The employee parked the tractor to service the mulcher
on an incline and was struck when it rolled backward, dragging him into the
field.  A coworker found the employee unresponsive under the tractor.  Emergency
Services responded and performed CPR while transporting the employee to the
hospital.  Injuries consisted of linear bruising to his upper chest and across
amputated and his second and third toes were partially amputated, requiring
medical treatment without hospitalization.
On January 8, 2020, an employee was working for a fuel oil dealer. He was the
firm's coowner. He was pumping fuel from a truck into a tank at a worksite. The
fuel wasn't flowing, so the employee crawled under the truck to open valves. His
clothes got caught in a PTO drive shaft. He sustained fatal injuries. He was
killed.
At 6:30 p.m. on January 4, 2020, an employee was walking while holding a raw
hamburger.  The employee tripped over a rack and attempted to break his fall

At 6:00 a.m. on December 14, 2019, an employee working as a temporary employee

hospitalization.
At 8:30 a.m. on January 4, 2020, an employee was working for a towing company.

employee and a coworker were tasked with helping to move windmill blades that

TL1055, Serial # OML500524 variable reach forklift. The employee was on the work
platform while the coworker operated the forklift to travel closer to the
location where the blades were to be placed. At some point during or immediately
after the platform traveled to the location, the employee fell out of the work

sustained multiple fractures including to his head, hip, and wrist. The employee
was hospitalized and treated for his injuries until he was discharged on

At 2:40 p.m. on July 17, 2019, Employee #1 and a coworker were removing nuts and

Employee #1 was removing metal sheeting from the roof, which had a pitch of
1:12.  He stepped backward and fell through a skylight.  The employee fell 16
feet head first and struck the concrete surface.  Employee #1 was killed.
At 4:30 p.m. on July 10, 2019, an employee was operating a belt sander deburring
a piece of metal when the motion of the sanding belt caused the piece to be
forced down in between the sanding belt and the tool rest. The employee's right
thumb was caught in the nip point as a result and amputated, requiring medical
treatment without hospitalization.
At approximately 8:00 a.m. on August 15, 2019, an employee was working and a
furnace blew up causing burns to the employee. The employee was taken to the
hospital and admitted for treatment of these injuries.
At 9:30 a.m. on January 2, 2020, an employee was working for a firm that
manufactured major household appliances. He was an electrician. He was replacing
a light bulb in the paint mixing room. The employee set up and climbed up on a
fiberglass extension ladder. As the employee was unscrewing the bulb, the

At 8:30 a.m. on January 2, 2020, an employee was making preparations to begin

The ladder slipped, and the employee held onto the edge of the roof. The
employee then fell to the ground when he couldn't hold on any longer. The
employee was hospitalized to treat a fractured back.
At 7:50 a.m. on July 11, 2019, an employee was cutting wooden floor panels with
a chain saw on the second floor of a building undergoing demolition and
alteration.  The employee had cut a line on the floor approximately 7 feet 9
inches. The employee tripped on debris and fell on other side of the line he had
just cut.  Three floor panels gave way, and the employee fell through them and
on to the first floor below.  The employee fell approximately 14 feet and was
hospitalized to treat unspecified injuries.
At 3:30 p.m. on November 20, 2019, an employee working as a carpenter for a
framing contractor was installing roof decking on a commercial building. The
employee slipped off a truss and fell to the concrete floor below. The employee
lacerated the right side of his head and bruised his right hip, requiring
hospitalization.
